function: Learns BS precoders, CRIS element transmission/reflection coefficients and modes, UAV position and speed, block lengths to maximize RSMA sum throughput under xURLLC constraints (pp. 3, 7).
system: BS with 4 antennas, four UAV-mounted CRIS units of 72 elements (8 per-element modes, incl. active STAR), 6 users with 3 antennas, RSMA, 2 GHz (pp. 2-4, 12).
method: Multi-agent DRL: PPO-based actor-critic with KL penalty, GAE and target networks, LSTM memory; one BS agent and one agent per UAV-CRIS, centralized value, trained by interaction (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulated Rician channels with Rayleigh NLoS, Doppler, path-loss exponents and norm-bounded CSI error in a 3D volume; online interaction, no 3GPP model or dataset (pp. 6, 12).
test_conditions: Online learning in the simulator; results sweep CRIS units, PE elements, users, receive antennas, block length, error rate, distance, perfect or imperfect CSI; no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 13-16).
baselines: Learned: DQN, DDPG, PPO, MADDPG, MAPPO; also eight RIS modes, SDMA/NOMA, with/without optimal CRIS phase, no-CRIS; no classical optimization baseline (pp. 13-16).
metrics: Sum throughput (bps/Hz), average reward per episode, individual data rate, packet error rate, reward variance over seeds (pp. 13-16).
complexity: Order O(K T (1+L q+M) + D T (1+M)) for interaction plus training, over episodes, steps, LSTM layers, agents, batch size; no runtime or FLOPs (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 6: "all the above channels follow the Rician fading distribution" with Rayleigh BS-user links, Doppler and path-loss exponents, a custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is used (Table II, p. 12).
q2_support: p. 13: "Unless we redefine the parameter with new values, the value remains fixed as given in Table II" introduces sweeps of users, antennas, CRIS units, block length and distance; no separate unseen-scenario test or adaptation is reported (pp. 13-16).
q3_support: p. 12: "As benchmarks, we compare our proposed LSTM-based MADRL algorithm against three popular DRL algorithms" and p. 14: "27.547 bps/Hz achieved by PPO" give learned baselines on throughput; no non-learned baseline is declared, and the only other reference, p. 13: "whether we account for optimal phase design for the PE elements in CRIS or ignore it", is never defined as a fixed or random configuration or an optimization algorithm.
q4_support: p. 12: "the total time complexity of the entire algorithm is" O(K T (1+L q+M) + D T (1+M)), derived in Section V-D (pp. 11-12); no runtime, FLOPs or parameter count is given.
q5_support: p. 12: "DDPG, and PPO algorithms are implemented using Python and TensorFlow" on a custom simulator (Table II); no code or data link is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Area 3 chosen over area 6: the learned physical-layer decisions are the BS precoders and the CRIS coefficients (p. 7); BS and users are terrestrial and the UAV only carries the RIS, so I did not treat it as NTN, which the reviewer may confirm. UAV position is learned jointly with them, so above_phy passes. Tables I to III (pp. 2, 12, 13) and Figs. 5 to 10 (pp. 13-16) were read from page images. q3 is 0 because no non-learned baseline is explicitly defined; the reviewer may check the without-optimal-phase curves of Fig. 6a (p. 14).
